Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:1.hebrew: אלא מתני' - לא מתוקמא אלא באדייה אדויי, שזרק התרנגול הדליל ושיבר בזריקתו כלים, דהוו צרורות, ואפילו קשרו אדם נמי לא משלם אלא ח"נ בעל התרנגול, והקושר פטור, שלא נתקל אדם בבורו. ודרב הונא לא מתוקמא אמתני', אלא בעלמא אתמר, והכי אתמר: דליל הפקר כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:1.english: Rather, the Mishnah - [It] is only established [as referring to a case] where [the rooster] flung [it], meaning that the rooster threw the string and broke vessels by throwing it, which is [categorized as] pebbles. And even if a person tied it, the owner of the rooster still only pays half-damages, and the one who tied [it] is exempt, since no person stumbled over his pit. And [the statement] of Rav Huna is not established on the Mishnah; rather, it was stated in general, and thus it was stated: "An ownerless string, etc."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:2.hebrew: נקשר מאליו - בתרנגול ונתקל בו אדם, פטור, דמאן ליחייב? דליל לית ליה בעלים; בעל התרנגול נמי — איש בור אמר רחמנא, ולא שור בור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:2.english: It was tied on its own - to a rooster, and a person stumbled over it, [the owner] is exempt, for who should be liable? The string has no owner; [and as for] the owner of the rooster as well, the Merciful One said "a man [who creates] a pit," and not "an ox [that creates] a pit."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:3.hebrew: קשרו אדם חייב - הקושר, דקנייה בהגבהה, ויש לו להאי דליל בעלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:10:3.english: If a person tied it, he is liable - The one who tied [it is liable], for he acquired it through lifting, and this string has an owner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:11:1.hebrew: משום מאי מחייב - דהא לאו בור מעליא הוא, שהרי לא הזיק במקום שקשרו שם, שהתרנגול גררו למקום אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:11:1.english: Due to what is he liable - For this is not a proper pit, since it did not cause damage in the place where he tied it, as the rooster dragged it to another place.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:11:2.hebrew: בורו המתגלגל - דמייתינן ליה בפ"ק (ד' ו.) בהצד השוה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:11:2.english: His pit that is rolled - Which we derive in the first chapter (6a) via [the principle of] "the common feature" [hatzad hashaveh].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:12:1.english: How is the tooth forewarned - And [the Mishnah] answers: To eat what is fit for it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:12:2.english: [It] pays half damages - For it is unusual.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:12:3.hebrew: אבל ברה"ר פטור - דבעינן "ובער בשדה אחר", ואכסות וכלים נמי פטור. בגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:12:3.english: But in the public domain [the owner] is exempt - For we require [the condition of] "and it shall consume in another's field." And for garments and vessels [the owner] is also exempt; in the Gemara it explains this.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:14:1.hebrew: מצדי הרחוב משלמת מה שהזיקה - כדין קרן — תם חצי נזק ומועד נזק שלם. ובגמ' מפרש לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:14:1.english: From the sides of the street, it pays what it damaged - According to the law of *keren* — [for] a *tam* [innocuous animal, it pays] half-damages, and [for] a *mu'ad* [forewarned animal, it pays] full damages. And in the Gemara it explains it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:14:2.hebrew: מה שנהנית - לאו תשלומין מעליא נינהו, כדמפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:14:2.english: What it benefited - This is not a full payment, as [it] explains in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:1.english: And a cow that ate barley - For it is the food of a donkey.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:2.hebrew: וחמור שאכל כרשינין - שהן מאכל פרה, וכן חזיר וכלב. ואע"ג דאינן רגילין בכך, הואיל ואורחייהו למיכלינהו ע"י הדחק כשהן רעבין, ראויין להן קרינן ביה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:2.english: And a donkey that ate vetches - For they are cow food, and similarly [the] pig and [the] dog. And even though they are not accustomed to this, since it is their way to eat them under duress when they are hungry, we call it "fit for them."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:3.english: Anything that is not typical for it - to eat all the time.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:4.hebrew: ואכלה ע"י הדחק - כלומר, ואורחיה למיכל ע"י הדחק כי הני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:4.english: And it eats [it] under duress - That is to say, it is its way to eat [it] under duress, like these [cases].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:5.hebrew: שמיה אכילה - ואפילו שלא ע"י הדחק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:5.english: [It] is considered eating - And even [when] not under duress.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:6.hebrew: שונרא דאכל תמרי - אורחיה למכלינהו ע"י הדחק, אבל כסות וכלים, אפילו ע"י הדחק לאו אורחיה למכלינהו, אלא מתכוין להזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:16:6.english: A cat that eats dates - It is typical for it to eat them under duress; however, [as for] clothing and utensils, even under duress it is not typical for it to eat them, rather it intends to cause damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:1.hebrew: ופלסיה - לעסו. לישנא אחרינא: פלסיה — סדקו, ולא שמעתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:1.english: And [it] broke it - Chewed it. Another explanation: palseih [means] cracked it, and I have not heard [this].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:2.hebrew: אסלא חצי נזק - דמשונה הוא. וכגון דתפס ניזק, דאין דנין דיני קנסות בבבל, ופלגא נזקא קנסא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:2.english: For the basket, half [the] damage - Because it is unusual [behavior]. And [this applies] where the injured party seized [it], for we do not adjudicate cases of fines in Babylonia, and half-damage is a fine.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:3.hebrew: אורחיה לפלוסי סלא - כשהוא לועס הפת, לועס הסל עמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:17:3.english: It is typical for it to break the basket - When it chews the bread, it chews the basket along with it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:18:1.hebrew: בחיה - שאין דרכה בפת אפילו ע"י הדחק, אבל חמור דרכו בכך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:18:1.english: An undomesticated animal - For its way is not [to eat] bread even under pressing circumstances, whereas a donkey's way is [to do] so.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:19:1.english: [Meat] that is roasted - Roasted [over] fire.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:19:2.english: With a deer - It is not a deer's normal manner [to eat] bread and meat.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:19:3.hebrew: ובפתורא - שעל השלחן אכלו, שאין דרכו בכך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:19:3.english: And at the table - That it ate it on the table, for that is not its normal way.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:1:1.hebrew: והא"ר יוחנן - לקמן בהאי פירקין (בבא קמא דף כו):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:1:1.english: But doesn't Rabbi Yochanan say - Later in this chapter (Bava Kamma 26).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:2:1.hebrew: אבל ברה"ר פטור - דבעינן "ובער בשדה אחר". ואכסות וכלים נמי פטור, בגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:2:1.english: But in the public domain [he is] exempt - For we require "and it feed in another's field" [Exodus 22:4]. And for garments and vessels [he is] also exempt; in the Gemara [it] explains it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:2:2.hebrew: כי קאמר רבי יוחנן - "אין חצי נזק חלוק", על חצי נזק דקרן קאמר, דכתיב "יחצון" ו"חצו" תרי זימני, לאפוקי ממאן דפריך לקמן: "ולא תהא קרן ברה"ר חייבת כלום מק"ו". אבל חצי נזק דצרורות לעולם פטור ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:2:2.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said - "[the payment of] half-damages is not differentiated," he said [it] regarding the half-damages of Horn, for it is written "they shall divide" [yechetzun] and "and they shall divide" [vechatzu] twice, to exclude [the view of] the one who raises an objection later [in the Gemara]: "Should Horn in the public domain not be liable for anything by an a fortiori inference?" However, [for] the half-damages of pebbles, [one is] always exempt in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:3:1.english: In the antechamber [akil’a] - An enclosure [parka] in front of the house.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:3:2.hebrew: כשכשה בזנבה מהו - אורחה הוא ופטורה ברה"ר, או לא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:3:2.english: [If it] swung its tail, what is [the law] - Is it its normal manner and it is exempt in the public domain, or not?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:3:3.hebrew: וכי יאחזנה - בעלה בזנבה וילך, ודאי פטור ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:3:3.english: Must he grasp it - [I.e.,] its owner, by its tail and walk? Certainly he is exempt in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:4:1.english: This is its typical behavior - And it is a subcategory of Foot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:5:1.english: He raised a dilemma [regarding] excessive [tail] swinging - Whether it is its typical behavior or not.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:7:1.english: They only taught - that [he pays] half-damages and nothing more.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:7:2.english: Only where [it] was tied on its own - [That is,] the string on the leg of the chicken.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:7:3.hebrew: אבל קשרו אדם חייב - הקושר נזק שלם, דהוי בור, ואם נתקל בו אדם, חייב בנזקו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:7:3.english: But if a person tied it, he is liable - The one who tied [it is liable for] full damages, for it is [categorized as] a Pit; and if a person stumbled over it, he is liable for his damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:1.english: [It] was tied on its own - [This refers to the case] of our Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:2.english: Who is liable - To pay half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:3.english: If [it is] the owner of the string - [meaning] that the rooster is not his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:4.hebrew: פושע הוא - וכוליה נזק בעי לשלומי, שהרי בורו הוא, שהשליכו לרה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:4.english: He is negligent - And he must pay the entire damage, for it is his pit, since he threw it into the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:5.hebrew: אלא דאצנעיה - בביתו, והוציאו תרנגול מביתו, וחייב בעל התרנגול:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:8:5.english: Rather, [it is] that he concealed it - in his house, and a rooster took it out of his house, and [thus] the owner of the rooster is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:9:1.hebrew: איש בור ולא שור בור - כי יכרה איש בור אמר רחמנא, ולא כי יכרה שור בור; והאי דליל, תרנגול כרהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 19b:9:1.english: A man [opens] a pit, and not an ox [opens] a pit - "When a man digs a pit," the Merciful One said, and not when an ox digs a pit; and [as for] this string, a chicken dug it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:1.hebrew: אלא מתני' בדאדייה אדויי - ואיירי בדליל הפקר או דחבריה ואצנעיה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:1.english: Rather, the Mishnah [refers to a case] where [the chicken] propelled it - And [the Mishnah] is dealing with an ownerless string, or [a string] of another person that [its owner] had put away:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:2.hebrew: וכי אתמר דרב הונא בעלמא אתמר - דלא מתוקמא אמתני', ד"קשרו אדם חייב" משמע הכל, ובדאדייה אדויי נמי חייב בעל תרנגול. ובקונטרס פי' דלא מתוקמא אמתניתין משום שהקושר היה פטור כיון דאדייה אדויי, שלא נתקל אדם בבורו. וקשה לפי': מ"מ ליחייב משום אשו, דהוי כאבנו וסכינו ומשאו שהניחן בראש גגו ונפלו ברוח מצויה והזיקו בהדי דאזלי; דהאי תרנגול הוי כרוח מצויה, מדפריך "אי דלא אצנעיה פושע הוא":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:2.english: And when Rav Huna's [statement] was stated, it was stated in a general [sense] - For it cannot be established as referring to the Mishnah, because [the statement] "if a person tied it, he is liable" implies [paying] the full [amount], and where [the chicken] flung it, the owner of the chicken is also liable [for half-damages]. And in the Kuntres [i.e., Rashi], he explained that it cannot be established as referring to our Mishnah because the one who tied [the string] would be exempt since [the chicken] flung it, for no person stumbled into his pit. And [this is] difficult according to his explanation: nevertheless, he [who tied it] should be liable on account of his Fire, for it is like his stone, his knife, and his burden that he placed on top of his roof and they fell in a common wind and caused damage while they were moving; for this chicken is like a common wind, [as is evident] from [the fact that the Gemara] asks, "If he did not put it away, he is negligent!"

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:3.english: "[If] it was tied on its own, he is exempt" - For [liability applies to] a person [who creates] a pit, and not an ox [that creates] a pit.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:4.hebrew: קשרו אדם חייב - לאו דוקא קשרו, דה"ה אם היה במקום המוצנע והניחו במקום התורפה שפשע בו, ואפי' לא הגביהו ולא קנאו; ודלא כמו שפירש הקונטרס דקני' בהגבהה כשקשרו, ויש לו להאי דליל בעלים. דכל תקלה שהניחה ברה"ר מיחייב ביה משום בור, אע"ג שלא זכה בה; דעד כאן לא פליגי רב ושמואל (לקמן בבא קמא ד' כח:) אלא בדלא אפקרי', אבל בדאפקרי' בין לרב בין לשמואל היינו בור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:10:4.english: "If a person tied it, he is liable" - Not specifically [where] he tied it, for the same applies if it was in a hidden place and he placed it in an exposed place such that he was negligent with it, even if he did not lift it and did not acquire it; and [this is] unlike what Rashi explained, that he acquires it through lifting when he ties it, so that this string has an owner. For [regarding] any obstacle that one placed in the public domain, he is liable for it under the category of bor [pit], even though he did not take possession of it; for Rav and Shmuel only disagree (below, Bava Kamma 28b) where he did not declare it ownerless, whereas where he declared it ownerless, according to both Rav and Shmuel it is [considered] a bor.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:16:1.hebrew: וחזיר שאכל חתיכה של בשר - אכילה ע"י הדחק היא, כדמסיק. והא דתנן גבי מדורות הנכרים, ומייתי לה בפרק קמא דפסחים (דף ט.): "כל מקום שחזיר וחולדה יכולין להלך אין צריכין בדיקה" — אומר ר"ת דשאני נפלים דרכיכי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:16:1.english: Or a pig that ate a piece of meat - This is eating under duress, as [the Gemara] concludes. And [as for] that which we learned in a Mishnah regarding the dwellings of gentiles, and [which the Gemara] cites in the first chapter of Pesachim (9a): "Any place where a pig or a weasel can go does not require searching [for chametz]" — Rabbeinu Tam says that aborted fetuses are different because they are soft.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:7:1.hebrew: אבל קשרו אדם חייב - פי': בתר דנייח, ומשום בור. ולאו דוקא קשרו, אלא כל היכא דלא אצנעיה — כקשרו דמי, כדקאמר: "אי דלא אצנעיה פושע הוא":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 19b:7:1.english: But if a person tied it, he is liable - Explanation: [This is] after [the string] came to rest, and [he is liable] on account of Pit. And [this applies] not specifically [where] he tied it; rather, wherever he did not put it away, it is considered as if he tied it, as [the Gemara] says: "If he did not put it away, he is negligent."
